system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

For every objection also fill `uae_basis`: if one of the UAE clauses shown (ids starting with ITU-UAE:, TDRA-,
UAE-, DXB-) speaks to this issue, set status "cites_uae" with its id and a word-for-word quote; otherwise set
status "none_applies" with empty ref and quote. Say "none_applies" honestly: it tells the regulator where UAE
texts are silent.

Execution When you are ready to launch the execution stage, you mobilize resources and start setting up the development environment, accessing the data, detailing the use case requirements, and developing the blueprint. You also set up agile project management working practices. Once data is made accessible, you begin data exploration activities to check for quality, representation, granularity to form a judgement on data usability. Typically, data quality dimensions cover completeness, accuracy, validity, consistency, timeliness, and uniqueness and accordingly some data cleansing activities might be required. Representation of the data is key for eliminating bias in AI models and to drive trust in the results. Accordingly, either more data needs to be collected from different sources (potentially including synthetic data) or you are ready to proceed with structuring and annotating the data. Data annotation and labeling can be a time-consuming exercise depending on the volume and sector-specific expertise required but is a critical step to prepare for model development and training.

data.summary: The alert states the end time as 21:00, but the verified NCM bulletin says conditions continue until 19:00. The hazard, wind, visibility and place details otherwise match the bulletin, and the unverified dam rumour is correctly left out.

objections.issue: The validity end time is wrong. The alert says 21:00 in both the headline and the description, but the NCM bulletin says conditions continue until 19:00. This extends the hazard window by two hours beyond what the bulletin supports.
objections.fix: Change the end time to 19:00 in the headline and the description, for example 'Dusty winds reducing visibility until 19:00 today' and 'Expected until 19:00 this evening, 4 March.'

evidence.quote: Dusty winds reducing visibility until 21:00 today

no_basis.concern: Certainty 'Observed' and urgency 'Immediate' appear consistent with the bulletin, which says conditions began at 14:55 and are ongoing. No CAP clause contradicts this.
no_basis.searched_for: CAP certainty Observed definition and NCM bulletin consistency
